newsitem.title: CHINA: RESEARCH ALERT - SALOMON GOES NEUTRAL ON HK.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - SALOMON GOES NEUTRAL ON HK.

text.p: Salomon Brothers Inc said it has reduced its weighting to neutral on Hong Kong.
"Our shift to neutral occurred before the Hang Seng index crossed 16,000," chief regional strategist Deep Kapur wrote in a research note.

"The float of the Thai baht, evidence of external sector recovery in Korea and high market volatility in Hong Kong dictated major changes to our market allocation on 2 July 1997. Hong Kong was reduced to neutral as part of these changes."

Salomon will remain neutral despite the continued surge in the Hang Seng, which would indicate a reduction to underweight, and a delay in the expected round of monetary tightening in the U.S., which would indicate an overweight position.

"Our investment methodology is primarily driven by considerations of relative value," Kapur said. "In reviewing our valuation models, we have not uncovered any compelling reason to change our investment stance."

The high transaction costs in Asian markets require that changes to relative value rankings must be large to warrant major moves in market allocation, whether on a tactical or strategic basis, Kapur said.
Four factors are critical in valuing the Hong Kong market from a "top-down" perspective: the short and long end of the yield curve, inflation and political risk.
Recent declines in U.S. bond yields and a reduction in political risk has been offset by higher interbank rates in Hong Kong, Kapur said.
